claims.text: The deviation on this trip is over tolerance, so POL-RD-24's two no-refund tolerance rows cannot be reached. The platform's own recorded distances on the trip record are 11.4 km actual against 10.0 km optimal, a deviation of 1.40 km, and the trip record's derived deviation block sets within_tolerance to false against POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance. Deviation of 1 km or less being absent, rows (c) and (e) are unavailable and the rider's case must be decided under row (a), (b) or (d) — that is, the charge stands only if the reroute was genuinely traffic-justified.

Traffic justification is not established on this record. POL-RD-23 justifies a reroute only where a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY both intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window. The advisory relied on (LTA-TI-260805-1205, an ACCIDENT on the CTE towards SLE after the Balestier Road exit) does overlap the trip window, but the artifact's own derived block returns null for intersects_route and for justifies_reroute and states in terms that 'the record does not say whether this advisory lies on the recommended route'. The element that would connect the advisory to THIS trip is therefore missing from the evidence, and the driver's in-app assertion of a jam ('CTE got accident after Balestier') cannot fill the gap, because POL-RD-23 requires the traffic data itself to intersect the recommended route. With the deviation over 1 km, POL-RD-24 row (d) applies and the excess distance fare is refundable in full.

The rider is still carrying the disputed charge and the sum row (d) returns is the excess distance fare: 1.40 km of deviation at 0.72 SGD per km, 1.01 SGD, with no surge applied (POL-RD-24's formula and its C3 note; the fare ledger's derived money block carries excess_distance_fare_sgd = 1.01). The ledger shows payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.0 and total_charged 22.60, so nothing has yet been returned. The rider's stated figure of 4.50 SGD is not the measure POL-RD-24 provides, and the rider does not press it; the rider-favourable outcome the policy gives is PARTIAL_REFUND of 1.01 SGD, which is part of this trip's charge returned.

On the contact obligation the rider does not contend otherwise. The chat log shows the driver's message at 18:57:46 and the rider's reply 'Ok sure, thanks for telling' at 18:58:26, both before the deviation detected at 19:00:36, which under POL-RD-21 confirms the rider's acknowledgment and makes this deviation an agreed one. That concession does not save the charge: POL-RD-24 row (a), the no-refund row, requires the reroute to be traffic-justified as well as agreed, and for the reasons above it is not; row (d) contains no notification element at all and refunds the excess distance fare whether or not the rider was told.

The detour the rider paid for did not deliver the saving the driver promised. The trip record shows the completed trip at 23.0 minutes against an optimal duration of 20.2 minutes, and 11.4 km against an optimal 10.0 km, so the rider bore both the extra distance and extra time of the Bendemeer Road detour. A reroute justified under POL-RD-23 is one the traffic data supports for the recommended route segment; nothing in the record shows this detour was the beneficial course, which is a further reason not to leave the excess distance on the rider.

If the judge is not persuaded either way on whether this advisory intersects the recommended route, then the very fact POL-RD-24's matrix turns on — whether the reroute was traffic-justified — cannot be established on this record, and POL-GEN-26 requires the case to be escalated rather than decided against the rider; POL-RD-25 licenses ESCALATE on a route deviation. On an escalation no monetary outcome issues and the amount is held, so the rider's 4.50 SGD claim is not finally refused on an evidentiary gap that is not the rider's to fill.

claims.text: POL-RD-21 requires the driver to inform the rider by in-app chat before or at the point of deviation, and the chat log shows exactly that. MSG-05003-003 was sent at 18:57:46 and delivered at 18:57:48, giving a brief reason (CTE accident after Balestier, very jam, exiting at Bendemeer, 'should be faster'); the platform did not record the deviation until 19:00:36, at the CTE / Bendemeer Road exit. The notice came almost three minutes before the point of deviation, so the contact obligation is met and the deviation is a notified one, not a silent reroute.

The same chat log carries the rider's acknowledgment. MSG-05003-004, sent 18:58:26 and read at 18:58:49, reads 'Ok sure, thanks for telling' - again before the 19:00:36 deviation. POL-RD-21 provides that where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment the deviation is agreed, and because the notice was given in writing there is no need for a call recording to establish it; no call recording is missing from this case because none was required.

The reroute was traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. The LTA advisory records an ACCIDENT on Central Expressway (CTE) towards SLE, after Balestier Road exit, valid 18:37:44 to 19:49:44, which brackets the whole trip window of 18:49:44 to 19:12:44 (overlaps_trip_window is true). ACCIDENT sits on POL-RD-23's admissible incident list, and the advisory's own road, Central Expressway (CTE), is one of the roads in the recommended route recorded at trip start. I put this no higher than the record allows: the derived block leaves 'on the recommended route' marked undetermined, so the intersection is argued from the advisory's road field matching the recorded recommended route, its window covering the trip, and its incident type being one the clause admits - not from anything outside the case file.

Those facts place this case squarely in row (a) of POL-RD-24: the reroute was traffic-justified, the rider was informed in-app before the deviation and acknowledged it, and the deviation was 1.40 km, above the 1.0 km tolerance. Row (a) provides no refund. The correct ruling is therefore NO_ACTION: the rider's claim is not supported and the present state stands. The fare breakdown shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so NO_ACTION preserves the 22.60 SGD the driver earned and moves nothing back to the rider.

Even if the Judge were to decline the traffic justification or the rider's agreement, no row of POL-RD-24 returns the 4.50 SGD the rider asks for. Rows (b) and (d) return only the excess distance fare: the deviation distance of 1.40 km times the per-km rate of 0.72 SGD, with no surge, rounded to the cent - that is 1.01 SGD. The rider's demand is more than four times the largest sum this category can move on this record, so FULL_REFUND of 4.50 SGD is unavailable on any view of the evidence.

What the rider is really complaining about - 'fare was higher than my usual ride home' - is the 4.55 SGD surge applied at a 1.30 multiplier, not the deviation. POL-RD-24 computes the excess distance fare from the per-km rate alone and applies no surge, so none of the surge enters a refund under this category. The deviation can move at most the 1.01 SGD excess distance fare, and the surge component is outside that computation entirely.

There is no escalation ground on this record. Every artifact this argument rests on - trip record, GPS trace, chat log, fare breakdown and traffic advisory - is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so POL-GEN-02's completeness requirement is met and no disclosure of impairment is owed. The facts the rules need (deviation distance, notice, acknowledgment, justification) are all established rather than missing, so POL-GEN-26 has no open question to send upstairs. The contested value is 4.50 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and driver_profile.fraud_flags is 0, so neither POL-GEN-22's raised bar nor POL-RD-25's confidence rule pulls this case to a human reviewer. The AI may and should decide it.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: this is trip TRP-05003 (5 Aug 2026, One Raffles Place to NEX, Serangoon), category ROUTE_DEVIATION, with 4.50 SGD contested. I applied POL-RD-21 to POL-RD-25 and the general policy.

1. The deviation. The platform's own recorded distances give 11.4 km actual against 10.0 km optimal - a deviation of 1.40 km (POL-RD-22), above the 1.0 km tolerance. Both advocates accept this, so POL-RD-24's tolerance rows (c) and (e) cannot apply.

2. Was the reroute traffic-justified? POL-RD-23 needs a traffic advisory that intersects the recommended route (Raffles Quay, CTE, Braddell Road, Upper Serangoon Road, Serangoon Central) and overlaps the trip window. The LTA advisory LTA-TI-260805-1205 records an ACCIDENT on the Central Expressway (CTE) towards SLE, after the Balestier Road exit, valid 18:37:44-19:49:44, which brackets the trip (18:49:44-19:12:44; overlaps_trip_window true). The CTE is the recommended route's main road, 'towards SLE' is the direction of travel, and the location after the Balestier Road exit lies on the CTE stretch the recommended route uses before it leaves the expressway at Braddell Road. The rider is right that the pre-pass field intersects_route was left blank and a blank field carries nothing by itself - but POL-RD-23 puts that determination to the Judge on the advisory's road, direction and location, and those place it on the recommended route. I find the reroute traffic-justified.

3. Was the rider informed and did the rider agree? The chat log shows the driver's message MSG-05003-003 at 18:57:46 ('CTE got accident after Balestier, very jam. I exit Bendemeer and go Upper Serangoon ok? Should be faster') and the rider's reply MSG-05003-004 at 18:58:26 ('Ok sure, thanks for telling'). Both precede the platform's recorded deviation at 19:00:36 at the CTE / Bendemeer Road exit, so notice came before the point of deviation and POL-RD-21 makes the deviation an agreed one.

4. Result. That places the case in row (a) of POL-RD-24 - traffic-justified, rider informed and agreed, deviation over 1 km - which provides no refund.

5. The money. The rider asks 4.50 SGD. Even if the reroute had not been justified, rows (b) and (d) return only the excess distance fare: 1.40 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.01 SGD (fare breakdown EV-FARE-05003, computed without surge). Neither 4.50 SGD nor the 4.55 SGD surge line is a sum POL-RD-24 can move, and the 23.0-minute versus 20.2-minute duration does not enter its formula.

6. No escalation. Every artifact relied on is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the facts POL-RD-24 turns on are established and POL-GEN-26 has no missing or impaired carrier to send upstairs. The contested value is 4.50 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD AI-final band, and there are no fraud or safety flags (POL-GEN-21), so POL-GEN-22 is satisfied and POL-RD-25's 0.80 confidence bar is met. No referral clause (POL-NS-22, POL-NS-24, POL-NS-25) applies.

Outcome: the rider's claim is not supported and the present state stands - the 22.60 SGD charged (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) is unchanged, and no amount is refunded to the rider or paid to the driver.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the rider's claim for 4.50 SGD back out of the 22.60 SGD metered fare on TRP-05003 is not supported, and the fare stands. The ruling is NO_ACTION, with both money fields null.

Deviation (POL-RD-22, v2.1 1.4): the platform's recorded distances are 11.4 km actual against 10.0 km recommended, a deviation of 1.40 km, over the 1.0 km tolerance. The rider's advocate is right that this takes rows (c) and (e) of POL-RD-24 (the within-tolerance no-refund rows) off the table.

Notification and agreement (POL-RD-21, v2.1 1.2): the driver messaged in-app at 18:57:46 with a brief reason ('CTE got accident after Balestier, very jam. I exit Bendemeer and go Upper Serangoon ok?'), before the deviation the platform recorded at 19:00:36, and the rider replied at 18:58:26, 'Ok sure, thanks for telling'. The rider was told before the point of deviation and acknowledged it, so this is an agreed deviation. The rider does not contest this and I accept it.

Traffic justification (POL-RD-23, v2.1 1.4): the LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-05003-01; type ACCIDENT, road Central Expressway (CTE), direction towards SLE, location after Balestier Road exit; valid 18:37:44-19:49:44) overlaps the trip window of 18:49:44-19:12:44. Read against the trip, its road is the Central Expressway, which the recommended route uses; its direction is the same northbound (towards SLE) direction the recommended route travels; and its location is on the CTE mainline before the recommended route leaves it, ahead of the Bendemeer exit the vehicle actually took. On its road, direction and location I find the advisory intersects the recommended route, so the reroute was traffic-justified. I do not accept the rider's argument that the advisory's blank intersects_route field leaves justification unestablished: that field is expressly left for the judge to decide from those three attributes, and all three point to intersection.

POL-RD-24 row (a) therefore applies - traffic-justified, rider informed and agreed, deviation over 1 km: no refund.

On the money (POL-RD-24, C3): the most this category could ever move on this record is the excess distance fare, 1.40 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 1.01 SGD with no surge (the fare ledger's excess_distance_fare_sgd is 1.01). The rider's 4.50 SGD demand, and his comparison with his usual fare, exceed any figure POL-RD-24 provides, and the 4.55 SGD surge at 1.30x sits outside the deviation formula entirely. The driver's further point, that the trip ran 23.0 minutes against an optimal 20.2 minutes, makes no difference either way: row (a)'s test is justification plus informed agreement, not whether the detour in fact saved time.

No escalation arises. The facts POL-GEN-26 needs - the deviation distance, the notification, the agreement and the traffic justification - are all established, from COMPLETE artifacts at weight_multiplier 1.0 (EV-TRIP-05003, EV-GPS-05003, EV-CHAT-05003, EV-FARE-05003, EV-ADVIS-05003-01), so the rider's fallback to POL-GEN-26 is not met. The contested value of 4.50 SGD is below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band and no fraud flag applies, so the AI may decide, and a confidence of 0.85 meets the 0.80 that POL-RD-25 requires (the 2 km limb of POL-RD-25 is not applied). No clause of the policy produces a referral, so none is made.

Its derived block leaves 'on the recommended route' undetermined and commits that determination to the judge on the advisory's road, direction and location. The reroute was therefore traffic-justified, and the rider's contrary argument (that the null intersects_route leaves justification unestablished) is rejected: POL-RD-23 assigns that determination to the judge, and the road, direction and location establish it. Outcome. POL-RD-24 row (a) applies — traffic-justified, rider informed and agreed, deviation over 1 km — so no refund issues. The rider's 4.50 SGD is not supported. For completeness, the most this category could ever have moved was the excess distance fare of 1.01 SGD (1.40 km × 0.72 SGD/km, no surge, per POL-RD-24 and the fare ledger's derived money block); that sum is not owed either, and the 4.55 SGD surge forms no part of the computation. The 22.60 SGD charge stands and no money moves.

Rider R-30760 filed this dispute over trip TRP-05003, charged 22.60 SGD, asking for 4.50 SGD back; driver D-96022 contests it. On the record the rider's claim is not supported, so the ruling is NO_ACTION: the 22.60 SGD charge stands and nothing is refunded.

Deviation (POL-RD-22). The platform's recorded distances on the trip record (EV-TRIP-05003) are 11.4 km actual against 10.0 km recommended, a deviation of 1.40 km. I exit Bendemeer and go Upper Serangoon ok? Should be faster') and the rider's reply MSG-05003-004 at 18:58:26 ('Ok sure, thanks for telling'). The platform recorded the deviation at 19:00:36. The notice was given before the point of deviation and the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment, so under POL-RD-21 the deviation is an agreed one. The rider's advocate concedes this and I accept it; both advocates' notification claims on POL-RD-21 are answered here.

Traffic justification (POL-RD-23). The LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-05003-01 records an ACCIDENT on the Central Expressway (CTE) towards SLE, after the Balestier Road exit, valid 18:37:44 to 19:49:44, which brackets the trip window of 18:49:44 to 19:12:44; ACCIDENT is on POL-RD-23's admissible incident list. The artifact itself leaves 'on the recommended route' undetermined, so I decide it from its road, direction and location against the trip, as POL-RD-23 directs: the road is the CTE, which is the road the recommended route itself uses; the direction is the direction of travel; and the Balestier Road exit lies on the CTE stretch the recommended route keeps to before turning onto Braddell Road. The advisory therefore intersects the recommended route and the reroute is traffic-justified. I reject the rider's argument that the null intersects_route and justifies_reroute fields leave justification unestablished, and I reject the rider's conditional request (POL-GEN-26, POL-RD-25) to escalate on that ground: there is no open question here, because the fact is established from the artifact's own road, direction and location.

Refund matrix (POL-RD-24). Traffic-justified, rider informed and agreed, deviation over 1 km is row (a): no refund. The rider's 4.50 SGD claim fails. I also reject the rider's fallback that row (d) returns 1.01 SGD: row (d) is the not-justified row and does not apply. Even on the rider's best view no row returns 4.50 SGD, so FULL_REFUND is unavailable on any reading. The rider's complaint that the fare was 'higher than my usual ride home' is largely the 4.55 SGD surge at a 1.30 multiplier (EV-FARE-05003); POL-RD-24 computes the excess distance fare from per-km rate alone with no surge, so the surge is outside any refund under this category, and the excess distance fare that could be moved is only 1.40 km x 0.72 = 1.01 SGD. The rider's point that the trip took 23.0 min against an optimal 20.2 min does not bear on the matrix.

Escalation and confidence. Every artifact relied on (trip record, GPS trace, chat log, fare breakdown, traffic advisory) is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so POL-GEN-02's completeness requirement is met and no disclosure of impairment is owed. POL-GEN-22 allows the AI to decide: the disputed value is 4.50 SGD, below the 10.00 SGD band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag, so no raised bar applies. Confidence is 0.85, above POL-RD-25's 0.80. No clause adds a referral (this is not a no-show, so POL-NS-22 and POL-NS-25 do not fire, and POL-NS-24's goodwill credit is not engaged).

Outcome: NO_ACTION. amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd are null; nothing is refunded to the rider and nothing is collected from the driver.

ledger.claim: The deviation on this trip is over tolerance, so POL-RD-24's two no-refund tolerance rows cannot be reached. The platform's own recorded distances on the trip record are 11.4 km actual against 10.0 km optimal, a deviation of 1.40 km, and the trip record's derived deviation block sets within_tolerance to false against POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance. Deviation of 1 km or less being absent, rows (c) and (e) are unavailable and the rider's case must be decided under row (a), (b) or (d) — that is, the charge stands only if the reroute was genuinely traffic-justified.

Traffic justification is not established on this record. POL-RD-23 justifies a reroute only where a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY both intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window. The advisory relied on (LTA-TI-260805-1205, an ACCIDENT on the CTE towards SLE after the Balestier Road exit) does overlap the trip window, but the artifact's own derived block returns null for intersects_route and for justifies_reroute and states in terms that 'the record does not say whether this advisory lies on the recommended route'. The element that would connect the advisory to THIS trip is therefore missing from the evidence, and the driver's in-app assertion of a jam ('CTE got accident after Balestier') cannot fill the gap, because POL-RD-23 requires the traffic data itself to intersect the recommended route. With the deviation over 1 km, POL-RD-24 row (d) applies and the excess distance fare is refundable in full.

The rider is still carrying the disputed charge and the sum row (d) returns is the excess distance fare: 1.40 km of deviation at 0.72 SGD per km, 1.01 SGD, with no surge applied (POL-RD-24's formula and its C3 note; the fare ledger's derived money block carries excess_distance_fare_sgd = 1.01). The ledger shows payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.0 and total_charged 22.60, so nothing has yet been returned. The rider's stated figure of 4.50 SGD is not the measure POL-RD-24 provides, and the rider does not press it; the rider-favourable outcome the policy gives is PARTIAL_REFUND of 1.01 SGD, which is part of this trip's charge returned.

On the contact obligation the rider does not contend otherwise. The chat log shows the driver's message at 18:57:46 and the rider's reply 'Ok sure, thanks for telling' at 18:58:26, both before the deviation detected at 19:00:36, which under POL-RD-21 confirms the rider's acknowledgment and makes this deviation an agreed one. That concession does not save the charge: POL-RD-24 row (a), the no-refund row, requires the reroute to be traffic-justified as well as agreed, and for the reasons above it is not; row (d) contains no notification element at all and refunds the excess distance fare whether or not the rider was told.

The detour the rider paid for did not deliver the saving the driver promised. The trip record shows the completed trip at 23.0 minutes against an optimal duration of 20.2 minutes, and 11.4 km against an optimal 10.0 km, so the rider bore both the extra distance and extra time of the Bendemeer Road detour. A reroute justified under POL-RD-23 is one the traffic data supports for the recommended route segment; nothing in the record shows this detour was the beneficial course, which is a further reason not to leave the excess distance on the rider.

If the judge is not persuaded either way on whether this advisory intersects the recommended route, then the very fact POL-RD-24's matrix turns on — whether the reroute was traffic-justified — cannot be established on this record, and POL-GEN-26 requires the case to be escalated rather than decided against the rider; POL-RD-25 licenses ESCALATE on a route deviation. On an escalation no monetary outcome issues and the amount is held, so the rider's 4.50 SGD claim is not finally refused on an evidentiary gap that is not the rider's to fill.

POL-RD-21 requires the driver to inform the rider by in-app chat before or at the point of deviation, and the chat log shows exactly that. MSG-05003-003 was sent at 18:57:46 and delivered at 18:57:48, giving a brief reason (CTE accident after Balestier, very jam, exiting at Bendemeer, 'should be faster'); the platform did not record the deviation until 19:00:36, at the CTE / Bendemeer Road exit. The notice came almost three minutes before the point of deviation, so the contact obligation is met and the deviation is a notified one, not a silent reroute.

The same chat log carries the rider's acknowledgment. MSG-05003-004, sent 18:58:26 and read at 18:58:49, reads 'Ok sure, thanks for telling' - again before the 19:00:36 deviation. POL-RD-21 provides that where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment the deviation is agreed, and because the notice was given in writing there is no need for a call recording to establish it; no call recording is missing from this case because none was required.

The reroute was traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. The LTA advisory records an ACCIDENT on Central Expressway (CTE) towards SLE, after Balestier Road exit, valid 18:37:44 to 19:49:44, which brackets the whole trip window of 18:49:44 to 19:12:44 (overlaps_trip_window is true). ACCIDENT sits on POL-RD-23's admissible incident list, and the advisory's own road, Central Expressway (CTE), is one of the roads in the recommended route recorded at trip start. I put this no higher than the record allows: the derived block leaves 'on the recommended route' marked undetermined, so the intersection is argued from the advisory's road field matching the recorded recommended route, its window covering the trip, and its incident type being one the clause admits - not from anything outside the case file.

Those facts place this case squarely in row (a) of POL-RD-24: the reroute was traffic-justified, the rider was informed in-app before the deviation and acknowledged it, and the deviation was 1.40 km, above the 1.0 km tolerance. Row (a) provides no refund. The correct ruling is therefore NO_ACTION: the rider's claim is not supported and the present state stands. The fare breakdown shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so NO_ACTION preserves the 22.60 SGD the driver earned and moves nothing back to the rider.

Even if the Judge were to decline the traffic justification or the rider's agreement, no row of POL-RD-24 returns the 4.50 SGD the rider asks for. Rows (b) and (d) return only the excess distance fare: the deviation distance of 1.40 km times the per-km rate of 0.72 SGD, with no surge, rounded to the cent - that is 1.01 SGD. The rider's demand is more than four times the largest sum this category can move on this record, so FULL_REFUND of 4.50 SGD is unavailable on any view of the evidence.

What the rider is really complaining about - 'fare was higher than my usual ride home' - is the 4.55 SGD surge applied at a 1.30 multiplier, not the deviation. POL-RD-24 computes the excess distance fare from the per-km rate alone and applies no surge, so none of the surge enters a refund under this category. The deviation can move at most the 1.01 SGD excess distance fare, and the surge component is outside that computation entirely.

There is no escalation ground on this record. Every artifact this argument rests on - trip record, GPS trace, chat log, fare breakdown and traffic advisory - is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so POL-GEN-02's completeness requirement is met and no disclosure of impairment is owed. The facts the rules need (deviation distance, notice, acknowledgment, justification) are all established rather than missing, so POL-GEN-26 has no open question to send upstairs. The contested value is 4.50 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and driver_profile.fraud_flags is 0, so neither POL-GEN-22's raised bar nor POL-RD-25's confidence rule pulls this case to a human reviewer. The AI may and should decide it.
